hints: Build the string one bracket at a time. What has to be true before you are allowed to write an opening bracket, and before a closing one?
An opening bracket needs two things: fewer than `n` opened so far, and fewer than `depth` still open. A closing one needs something open to close.
Those counters are the whole state - and checking them *before* recursing means every string you finish is valid, so nothing has to be filtered afterwards.

The recursion carries the string so far and the two counters. Each call tries an opening bracket if the rules allow one, then a closing bracket if they allow one, and a string of full length is an answer. There is no filtering step at the end.
